visual_anatomy.title: A three-line instructional title isolates two uppercase rough-display phrases in lavender tags, followed by a short statement about using a full colour spectrum.
visual_anatomy.layout: A nine-row controlled comparison: three brightness bands each contain low-, mid-, and high-saturation test strips. The same rainbow colour sequence and overlay text repeat in every strip, with a simple verdict at the far right.
visual_anatomy.reading_order: Headline → brightness section label → compare the three saturation rows within that section → read the concise verdict → repeat for the next brightness level.
visual_anatomy.typography: Light sans title, rough-display emphasised words, bold all-caps section labels, plain row labels, and one consistent sentence rendered directly over every test strip.
visual_anatomy.colour: The controlled variable is a full horizontal rainbow spectrum; brightness and saturation change across rows while the surrounding page remains white and restrained.
visual_anatomy.surface: Rounded spectrum bars with thin black outlines, mild shadows, black or white overlay text, and no illustration beyond the controlled colour experiments.
visual_anatomy.modules: Three brightness sections multiplied by three saturation rows, each with the same colour test, textual overlay, and qualitative verdict.
visual_anatomy.density: Moderate: repetition is intentional because it lets the reader see a visual condition rather than take the conclusion on trust.

transferable_mechanism.reader_job: See the effect of a variable under controlled changes rather than receive an abstract design rule.
transferable_mechanism.argument_shape: Repeated visual experiment across two comparison dimensions.
transferable_mechanism.mechanism: Keep the sample, text, and layout constant; vary only the named conditions in a stable grid so the visual difference itself becomes the evidence being discussed.
transferable_mechanism.use_condition: Use when the reader can actually inspect a controlled difference. For operational or quantitative claims, label the variables, source the data, and avoid substituting aesthetics for evidence.

anti_copy_boundary: Do not reuse the premium-colours subject, rainbow-strip experiment, exact brightness/saturation grid, headline wording, lavender rough-display tags, overlay sentence, verdict labels, or source palette treatment.
